component.name: Icon
component.description: Renders one of 22 inline SVGs from the fixed icon set. Uses currentColor so it inherits the surrounding text color. Size is controlled via size.icon.* tokens.

useWhen: Providing a visual cue alongside a label (Button leading icon, form field prefix)
Indicating direction or action in a compact space (chevrons, plus, minus)
Communicating theme state (sun/moon-star for light/dark toggle)

Opening an overflow menu of secondary actions (more-vertical, the vertical-ellipsis 'kebab'); always inside an icon-only Button with an aria-label and aria-haspopup="menu", never as a bare clickable glyph

notFor.case: Adding icons outside the fixed set
notFor.because: The set is intentionally small. Adding arbitrary icons bloats the bundle and fragments the visual language.
notFor.note: Choose the closest existing icon, or propose expanding the fixed set deliberately.

patterns.name: icon-label-pair
patterns.description: An Icon followed by a Text label inside an Inline, used for navigation items and feature callouts.

useWhen.sm: 16px — use inside dense UI elements such as tags, badges, or inline metadata.
useWhen.md: 24px — default; use alongside body text, in buttons, and as standalone affordances.

rules.case: Using Icon as the sole accessible label for an interactive control
rules.because: aria-hidden=true by default; a visually icon-only button has no accessible name.
rules.do: Pass the label prop to set aria-label, or wrap in a Button with a visually-hidden text label.

rules.case: Setting a color prop or inline style directly on the Icon element
rules.because: Icon uses currentColor — color must be set on the ancestor element that owns the color context, using a semantic token. IconProps currently only omits 'children' from the spread SVGAttributes type, so color, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, role, aria-hidden, and aria-label can all be passed through and silently override Icon's intended behavior with no type error.
rules.do: Apply the token via style or CSS on the ancestor span/element, never on <Icon> itself. Token choice depends on context: use color.icon.default for standalone or button-adjacent icons; use color.icon.subtle when the icon appears inline alongside color.text.subtle or metadata-scale text, so the icon sits in the same visual register as its label.
